formal_statement.lean_header:
theorem p01_t2_pairwise_vs_recursive_bounds
    (fp : StandardAddModel) (r : ℕ) (v : Fin (2 ^ r) → ℝ)
    (hvalid : GammaValid fp.u (2 ^ r - 1)) :
    |pairwiseSum fp.fl_add r v - ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), v i| ≤
        gamma fp.u r * ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), |v i| ∧
    |recursiveSum fp.fl_add (2 ^ r) v - ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), v i| ≤
        gamma fp.u (2 ^ r - 1) * ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), |v i| ∧
    gamma fp.u r ≤ gamma fp.u (2 ^ r - 1)
formal_statement.plain_language: Prove the pairwise bound, the recursive bound, and that the pairwise bound's gamma coefficient is no larger.

assumptions: There are exactly 2^r real inputs; their signs are unrestricted.
Each rounded addition follows the shared standard addition rule.
The shared recursiveSum definition copies the first input exactly. It does not call rounded addition from zero; that separate model field is kept only for the common interface and library adapters.
Overflow, underflow, and other exceptional machine behavior are outside the mathematical model.
informal_statement: For the same 2^r inputs, give both certified forward-error bounds and prove that gamma(u,r) is no larger than gamma(u,2^r-1).
informal_proof: Use equation (3.6) for the pairwise computation and equation (2.6) for the left-to-right computation. Prove r <= 2^r-1; the larger validity condition then also validates r. Since gamma is nondecreasing in its index in the valid range, the pairwise coefficient is no larger.
interpretation_warning: The last conjunct compares certified upper bounds only. It does not claim that the actual pairwise error is no larger than the actual recursive error for every input.
tier_rationale: The task combines two different paper estimates with an index inequality, a smaller validity condition, and a monotonicity step for gamma. No single theorem is the exact requested conjunction.
